etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English techere, equivalent to teach +‎ -er. More at teach.

definitions.definition: A person who teaches, especially one employed in a school; preceptor.

quote.citation: 2013 July 19, Mark Tran, “Denied an education by war”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 6, page 1:
quote.text: One particularly damaging, but often ignored, effect of conflict on education is the proliferation of attacks on schools […] as children, teachers or school buildings become the targets of attacks. Parents fear sending their children to school. Girls are particularly vulnerable to sexual violence.

quote.citation: 2017 February 28, Steve LeVine, “Trump Speech to Congress: The Message Was Trumpian, But The Tone Was Decidedly Not”, in Quartz‎[1]:
quote.text: But if the last two years are a teacher, look for the bombastic tweets to resume before sunrise.

definitions.definition: (Mormonism) The second highest office in the Aaronic priesthood, held by priesthood holders of at least the age of 14.
